c74object.name: evi_ringmod
c74object.digest: evieve Gen Object. Antialiased nonlinear ring modulator
c74object.description:
evi_ringmod is an abstraction for using inside gen~ or GenExpr.
evi_ringmod.gendsp requires the GenExpr file(s):
evi_ringmod_enhanced.genexpr
evi_ringmod is also available in MSP as: evi.ringmod~.
A clean FIR ring modulator algorithm with sine shaping saturation and filtering. Ring modulates two audio signals producing one modulated output, with antiderivative antialiasing and oversampling options.

geninlet.name: audio
geninlet.digest: Input 1. The first audio signal to be ring modulated (Carrier).

geninlet.name: audio
geninlet.digest: Input 2. The second audio signal to be ring modulated (Modulator).

attribute.name: cutoff
attribute.description: The object offers a utility Butterworth Lowpass on it's output for taming the distortion and high frequencies. This is the cutoff frequency of that filter. By default the filter is bypassed. See the @order attribute for details.

attribute.name: drive
attribute.description: Drive the waveshaping input gain via a sine shaping function. A bit like a % 0..1.. up to 2 is pretty safe, up to 4 be careful (in terms of aliasing).

attribute.name: highpass
attribute.description: This applies a highpass to the initial ring modulated audio mix, for taming bass response. It is not smoothed and thus probably best used as a static tool only.

attribute.name: order
attribute.description: The object offers a utility Butterworth Lowpass on it's output for taming the distortion and high frequencies. 0 (the default) = bypassed (and CPU off), 1..8 = filter orders 1..8 (increasing in steepness of slope). The cutoff of this filter is set with the @cutoff attribute.

attribute.name: quality
attribute.description: 0=1x/Adaa1, 1=1x/Adaa2, 2=4x/Adaa2, 3=8x/Adaa2. Because of the fake oversampling used here, higher and higher orders very slightly change the tonal effect of the audio output, so experimenting with different settings is not just about antialiasing or managing CPU usage but also a musical choice.

attribute.name: topology
attribute.description: The placement of the waveshaper in the ring modulator audio chain. If 0 (the default), the waveshaper sits after the ring modulator stage, if 1, the waveshaper is placed into the middle of the ring modulator. Option 1 gives a strongly clipped and 'squeezed' guitar-like output. Option 0 gives a more usual soft saturated output.
